transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-08-11
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 57 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Nina (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Jillian (Redwood CSM), Omar (Redwood), Lydia (Apogee), Tom (Apogee), Priya (Apogee), Marcus (Apogee Sec)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align on POC timeline/milestones, success criteria, required access, benchmark plan (latency / cost / quality), and coordination for the mid-point review and exec readout. Several security questions and a request for a benchmark template.

Topics:
- POC milestones and gate criteria
- Access & infra needs (VPC/VPN, service accounts, sample data)
- Workload sizing and traffic profile
- Benchmarks (latency p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, accuracy/QA metrics)
- Timeline and readout cadence

Action item recap (quick): see action_items field above.

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Nina (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side — I'm Nina, AE for the account, with Marco SE and Jillian CSM. how's everyone doing?
[00:14] Lydia (Apogee): Hi Nina, good thanks. Lydia here. excited to get this scoped out. we've been looking at Redwood for a bit — trying to understand the actual production economics and latency tradeoffs.
[00:29] Marco (Redwood SE): Awesome. high level today: want to agree the POC gates — kickoff, access setup, midpoint benchmark, and exec readout — and make sure we have what we need to run realistic tests.
[00:43] Tom (Apogee): Quick clarifier — when you say "realistic tests" do you mean full traffic replay? or a synthetic load? we can do both but want to know what you expect.
[00:55] Marco (Redwood SE): Great question. ideally we run a small replay of production-like traffic for functional correctness + quality checks, then a synthetic ramp for stress/latency. the benchmark spreadsheet we'll share has recommended ramp profiles.
[01:12] Priya (Apogee Product): For success criteria, our PM org will want cost per active user and end-to-end 95th percentile latency under 400ms for short completions. is that a reasonable SLO to try for?
[01:26] Nina (Redwood AE): That's reasonable as a target for hosted API routes if sequence lengths are low — we'll validate once we see token distribution. For dedicated / private VPC things change; we should capture both.
[01:40] Marcus (Apogee Sec): On security, we'll need SOC2 artifact and KMS integration details. also curious about audit logs and SSO. can you confirm Redwood supports customer-managed KMS in the private deploy?
[01:52] Marco (Redwood SE): Yes — private deployments support customer KMS/HSM and we can point to our audit log format. for hosted we have encryption at rest and TLS, plus SSO (SAML) for console access. I'll attach the security deck.
[02:06] Lydia (Apogee): Ok, good. timeline wise, we need a 4-week POC max; exec readout scheduled with our VP on 2027-09-10. so we need midpoint by end of August.
[02:18] Nina (Redwood AE): Noted. proposed POC: week 0 kickoff & access, week 1 baseline + integration, week 2 run benchmark sprints, week 3 mid-point review, week 4 stabilization + exec readout prep.
[02:32] Tom (Apogee): That aligns. can you describe the tooling you'll provide for benchmarks? like is there a harness we run or do you run it from Redwood side?
[02:45] Marco (Redwood SE): We provide a benchmark harness (python scripts + k6 templates) and a template Google Sheet. customer can run locally into the Redwood hosted endpoints or we can run inside a dedicated test environment if you prefer. for private redeploys we typically run on prem with our ops guidance.
[03:00] Marcus (Apogee Sec): Do you have a list of ports, IP ranges, and service accounts needed for VPC peering? our security team needs that up front.
[03:11] Omar (Redwood): We'll share a network access checklist; for VPC peering you'll need an account-level CIDR and we provide egress IPs. I'll add that to the runbook.
[03:23] Lydia (Apogee): Workload sizing: we have about 1.2k concurrent users at peak, average request size ~120 tokens, peak RPS around 80. we'll send you the sample traces.
[03:36] Marco (Redwood SE): Perfect — that token distribution will tell us whether quantized variants are feasible and whether batching will help cost. for 120 token requests, continuous batching can give big wins but depends on latency SLOs.
[03:49] Priya (Apogee): Can you explain how batching interacts with 95th p95 latency — sometimes batching hurts tail latency.
[03:58] Marco (Redwood SE): Right. there's a tradeoff: larger batch sizes increase throughput and lower cost per token, but if traffic is spiky it can increase p95. Our runtime supports dynamic batching with a max-latency bound so we can cap wait time to preserve p95. We'll propose three profiles in the spreadsheet: low-latency (small batch), balanced, and cost-optimized.
[04:18] Lydia (Apogee): For success criteria, we want two buckets: technical (p50/p95 latency, token cost, error rate) and business (P50 cost per MAU, model quality on our eval set).
[04:29] Nina (Redwood AE): Agreed. we'll map each gate to measurable metrics and thresholds in the POC runbook.
[04:35] Tom (Apogee): About models — do you support multiple model variants? we may want a smaller quantized model for cost testing and a larger one for quality checks.
[04:45] Marco (Redwood SE): Yes, our catalog has verified variants. we can test 3 variants: base FP16, 8-bit quantized, and distilled. We'll include model compatibility notes — sometimes tool calling or function outputs vary by variant and we should watch for delta in the eval metrics.
[04:59] Priya (Apogee): On metrics for quality, we'll seed your eval harness with our top 200 prompts and expected outputs. what's the format?
[05:07] Marco (Redwood SE): JSONL pairs (prompt, expected) works best. also include tolerance thresholds for fuzzy matching, BLEU/F1 or custom scoring.
[05:18] Lydia (Apogee): For the exec readout, what level of slides do you typically provide? we need an example deck showing cost curves and runbook recommendations.
[05:27] Jillian (Redwood CSM): We do an exec-ready deck — 6–8 slides: objectives, methodology, key results (latency/cost/quality), recommended deployment mode, risks, and next steps. We'll align that to your VP audience.
[05:40] Tom (Apogee): Any hidden infra costs? like GPU hours for dedicated testing?
[05:47] Nina (Redwood AE): For the POC we include benchmark compute in the scope — unless you ask for a full dedicated capacity run for sustained throughput, which would be quoted separately. We'll call out any billable items up front.
[05:58] Marcus (Apogee Sec): A few security items: data residency, retention policy for logs, and whether model inputs are used for training. we need explicit confirmation that hosted mode does not feed customer data into model training.
[06:10] Marco (Redwood SE): We have a strict policy: hosted inference for enterprise customers can be configured to opt out of any training data retention. for private deployments you're fully isolated. We'll share the data handling statement.
[06:22] Lydia (Apogee): Ok. let's walk through the milestone gates and acceptance criteria out loud so we all agree.
[06:30] Nina (Redwood AE): Gate 0: Kickoff & access — success if service accounts, VPC peering (if needed), sample payloads, and benchmark spreadsheet are in place. Gate 1 (end week 1): Baseline integration — SDK/requests work, basic quality checks pass. Gate 2 (end week 2): Benchmark sprint — run synthetic and replay tests, collect p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, and quality delta. Gate 3 (midpoint review week 3): We review results, decide on tuning or pivot. Gate 4 (exec readout week 4): Finalized runbook and recommendation.
[07:10] Tom (Apogee): For Gate 2, what percent variance is acceptable on quality relative to baseline?
[07:18] Priya (Apogee): we were thinking less than 3% top-level metric drop on our eval.
[07:23] Marco (Redwood SE): We can set thresholds per metric in the spreadsheet. note that quantized models might show larger deltas for certain tasks. we'll flag those in the model notes.
[07:32] Lydia (Apogee): If something fails Gate 2, do we get an optional extension?
[07:36] Nina (Redwood AE): Yes, there's a mutual decision. common path is an extra week for tuning or to test dedicated capacity. we'll include extension options in the runbook.
[07:47] Priya (Apogee): Regarding monitoring — what observability do you expose during the POC?
[07:53] Omar (Redwood): We provide per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, and tracing hooks. You can also ship logs to your SIEM. We'll give read-only console access to your engineering leads.
[08:06] Marcus (Apogee Sec): Will the console access be via SSO? We require SAML + RBAC.
[08:11] Marco (Redwood SE): Yes we support SAML and fine-grained RBAC. we'll capture the user list for provisioning.
[08:20] Lydia (Apogee): About benchmarks: can you explain how you measure "cost per 1k tokens" — is that just invoice cost or a modeled unit including batching effects?
[08:30] Marco (Redwood SE): It's modeled based on tokens consumed and effective GPU utilization during the benchmark, so it reflects batching/caching benefits. we'll show both raw token billing and effective per-call cost.
[08:42] Tom (Apogee): Any recommendations for the eval set size?
[08:46] Marco (Redwood SE): 500–2,000 prompts is a good range; pick representative samples across your key intents. we'll compute n-gram and embedding-based similarity to detect regressions.
[08:58] Lydia (Apogee): On replay: we'll sanitize PII and share traces; can you support header-preserving replay so we can test routing logic?
[09:08] Marco (Redwood SE): Yes, replay harness has an option to preserve headers and session IDs. we'll coordinate the schema.
[09:18] Priya (Apogee): For the mid-point review, what artifacts should we expect?
[09:24] Jillian (Redwood CSM): Mid-point packet: raw benchmark CSVs, summary deck (1–2 slides), error rate breakdown, and a list of tuning suggestions.
[09:33] Tom (Apogee): About latency SLOs: if we can't meet p95 <400ms, do you recommend dedicated or private deployment?
[09:41] Marco (Redwood SE): It depends on traffic shape and model. Dedicated usually helps because you avoid noisy neighbors and can pick hardware. Private gives you the most control but has longer lead time. We'll model both in the spreadsheet.
[09:54] Lydia (Apogee): Who will run the first benchmark run — Redwood or Apogee?
[09:58] Nina (Redwood AE): We prefer you run the initial replay to validate integration; Redwood will run the synthetic stress runs and a cross-check. we'll include step-by-step commands.
[10:10] Tom (Apogee): Ok, logistics — where do we upload sample traces? Github private repo or S3?
[10:16] Nina (Redwood AE): S3 is easiest. we'll share a pre-signed link and upload instructions.
[10:24] Marcus (Apogee Sec): Minimal access principle — only service accounts, no long-lived keys.
[10:29] Omar (Redwood): Agreed. we'll provide short-lived creds and a service account with least privilege.
[10:36] Lydia (Apogee): A small question on caching: do you provide prefix/KV caching? we have some heavy reused context that could be cached.
[10:44] Marco (Redwood SE): Yes we support prefix and KV cache patterns. for chat workloads with repeated context it can dramatically cut token decode. we'll add recommended cache TTLs in the runbook.
[10:54] Priya (Apogee): If we do private deployment, how long does provisioning take?
[10:58] Marco (Redwood SE): Typical private deployment is 4–8 weeks depending on host ops and network approvals. for a POC we normally use hosted or a short-lived dedicated pool to keep things fast.
[11:09] Lydia (Apogee): Great. let's confirm dates: POC start next Monday 2027-08-16?
[11:14] Nina (Redwood AE): We can do 2027-08-16 kickoff. that gives us time to share runbook on Friday.
[11:20] Tom (Apogee): Midpoint review — we prefer 2027-09-01 in the morning. does that work?
[11:25] Jillian (Redwood CSM): yep marking that. exec readout 2027-09-10 per Lydia's note.
[11:32] Marcus (Apogee Sec): A few follow-ups — we need the security deck, network checklist, and the data handling statement.
[11:38] Marco (Redwood SE): I'll attach the security deck and network checklist. expect those by 2027-08-13.
[11:44] Lydia (Apogee): One more thing — do you have a recommended rollback/fallback strategy if model quality regresses in production?
[11:50] Marco (Redwood SE): Yes, we recommend model pinning, automatic fallback to a conservative variant, and canary rollout policies for gradual traffic shift. we'll document those in the runbook.
[12:01] Priya (Apogee): For the benchmark sheet, would like columns for scenario name, model variant, batch config, p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, accuracy metric, notes.
[12:12] Marco (Redwood SE): That's the exact layout we use. we'll send the template.
[12:18] Nina (Redwood AE): Ok folks — quick recap of who does what: Redwood sends runbook + benchmark template + security deck by Friday (2027-08-13). Apogee to send payloads, traces, and token distribution by Tuesday (2027-08-16). Redwood to provision test harness and run initial synthetic run (due 2027-08-18). Midpoint review scheduled 2027-09-01. Exec readout 2027-09-10.
[12:44] Lydia (Apogee): Sounds good. any blockers we should surface now?
[12:49] Marcus (Apogee Sec): We'll need the SOC2 artifact and a KMS integration plan to sign off networking.
[12:56] Nina (Redwood AE): We'll include SOC2 and KMS docs in the security packet.
[13:03] Tom (Apogee): Logistics — who should we loop into Slack or email alias for day-to-day?
[13:08] Jillian (Redwood CSM): We'll create an alias redwood-apogee-poc@ and a slack channel for the team.
[13:15] Priya (Apogee): OK thanks everyone. look forward to the template.
[13:19] Nina (Redwood AE): Thanks all. we'll follow up with the doc links and next steps.
[13:24] Marco (Redwood SE): Bye everyone.
[13:27] End of call

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings on proper nouns (e.g., "prefix cache" sometimes transcribed as "pre-fix cache"), and speaker labels were manually normalized. There may be small punctuation/parsing artifacts in the transcript.
